term_id: # Generic rows of the English target (all works). Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions
source_pattern: flags iu; they must not contain commas (write \x2C). The source pattern is matched against the source paragraph (Latin or Greek: the printed spellings i/j and u/v are both covered)
target_pattern: the target pattern against the translation of the same paragraph. All rows are PROPUS until a reviewer of the tradition approves them.

note: gratia → grace. Not "favour" or "mercy" (misericordia → mercy). "gratias agere" (to give thanks) is not matched on purpose.

iustitia → righteousness (the default in works on grace and the law) or justice (the distributive or forensic sense). Context decides; keep one choice per passage and flag the doubtful ones AMBIGUITATE.
iustificare → to justify; iustificatio → justification.
lex → law. Beware of legere (to read): legis/lege/legem are also forms of that verb; the law of Moses is "the Law" when it is the Mosaic Law as a whole.
spiritus → spirit or Spirit. "Spirit" (capital) for the Holy Spirit and the Spirit of God; "spirit" for the human spirit; the adjective spiritalis → spiritual. Flag a doubtful case AMBIGUITATE.
Spiritus Sanctus → the Holy Spirit. Never "Holy Ghost" (see holy-ghost-forbid).
Archaism; "Holy Spirit" (see spiritus-sanctus).
littera → the letter (2 Cor. 3:6
column9: the letter that kills); iuxta litteram → literally or according to the letter. litterae can also be an epistle or writings: "letter" still holds.

note: fides → faith (trust or fidelity where the context is not about believing).
caritas → love; "charity" only where the profile asks for it. Keep apart dilectio (love; delight in the one loved) and amor.
peccatum → sin; peccator → sinner; peccare → to sin. The rendering is the word itself and its family (sins
column14: not any word that starts with the letters: since
column15: single and sincere are not sin.

note: liberum arbitrium → free will (some scholarly translations say "free choice"; use it only if the profile of the work asks for it).
voluntas → will (the faculty); voluntas Dei → the will of God. Not "wish" unless the context is a wish.
praedestinatio → predestination; praedestinare → to predestine.
sacramentum is wider than "sacrament" (sign; mystery; oath). Decide in context and keep the Latin only if the profile asks.
ecclesia → the Church (capital) for the whole Church; a church (lower case) for a local community or a building.
episcopus → bishop.
trinitas → the Trinity.
baptismus → baptism.
mediator → Mediator (Christ; 1 Tim. 2:5).
concupiscentia → concupiscence in the technical sense (Augustine); "covetousness" or "desire" where the text quotes Rom. 7:7 (concupiscentiam nesciebam). Decide once per work.
ὁμοούσιος → of one substance with (the Father); also consubstantial. The central term of the Creed of Nicaea. Never "of like substance" (ὁμοιούσιος).
ὑπόστασις → hypostasis (technical) or person; in older texts (Nicaea 325) the word is a synonym of οὐσία → substance. Decide in context and flag AMBIGUITATE.
οὐσία → essence or substance; one choice per work.
θεοτόκος → Mother of God (or the God-bearer; Theotokos left in Greek only if the profile asks).
Modern scholarly English: no archaisms. Scripture quoted by the author is translated as the author's text
